item.title: [39★] Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
item.author: Chao Yin, Vedika Khemani
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 39 ★

Authors: Chao Yin, Vedika Khemani

arXiv ID: 2611.17433 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct O(1)\mathrm{O}(1)-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with O(1)\mathrm{O}(1)-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a Ω(1)\Omega(1) spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the qq-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any qq and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional Z2\mathbb{Z}_2 lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.

Chao Yin, Vedika Khemani

item.title: [36★] Efficient representations by PEPS: critical free-fermion and chiral topological states
item.author: Ignacio Cirac, Rahul Trivedi
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 36 ★

Authors: Ignacio Cirac, Rahul Trivedi

arXiv ID: 2611.17936 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We construct projected entangled-pair state (PEPS) approximations to various many-body states in 2D lattices with global error at most ϵ\epsilon and bond dimension polynomial in the system size and 1/ϵ1/\epsilon. They include critical free-fermion models in two dimensions, as well as chiral topological states. For the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor tight-binding model at half filling, our construction combines Gaussian wavelet transformations with matrix product state approximations of the one-dimensional chains, as well as selected fermionic swap operations. For arbitrary uniformly gapped, finite-range quadratic Hamiltonians, we give a different construction based on repeated one-particle filtering, which yields Gaussian PEPS in any spatial dimension. Those include, for instance, p+ipp+ip models or a Chern-insulator in a square lattice, for which we give an explicit construction. Finally, we prove that Gutzwiller projections of a fixed number of identical Gaussian PEPS approximations to free-fermion states at arbitrary filling do not amplify considerably the approximation error. This provides a polynomial-bond PEPS approximations to the resulting states, including familiar lattice chiral-spin-liquid states.

Ignacio Cirac, Rahul Trivedi

item.title: [26★] Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
item.author: Aritra Lahiri, Florian Marquardt
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 26 ★

Authors: Aritra Lahiri, Florian Marquardt

arXiv ID: 2611.18504 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Scaling quantum computing toward practical quantum advantage is currently limited by the efficiency of circuits that operate on information encoded by quantum error-correcting codes. The full stack of quantum computing encompasses several tasks: preparation of logical code states, implementation of logical gates, logical routines on encoded qubits, etc. Yet, these circuits are largely designed by hand for individual cases, with some recent works incorporating machine learning for certain aspects. We formulate this problem as agentic evolutionary program synthesis, wherein a large language model, leveraging its pretraining knowledge and tool-use proficiency, and guided by a circuit verifier, evolves a program that defines a Clifford circuit for a wide range of curated tasks such as logical state preparation, logical gate design, and logical routines such as code-switching, code growth, etc. Our approach consistently finds fault-tolerant circuits for all of these tasks, each verified by an exhaustive check over faults.

Aritra Lahiri, Florian Marquardt

item.title: [23★] Quantum phase estimation on a Rydberg quantum simulator
item.author: Hendrik Timme, ..., Immanuel Bloch, Johannes Zeiher
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 23 ★

Authors: Hendrik Timme, ..., Immanuel Bloch, Johannes Zeiher

arXiv ID: 2611.18122 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Determining the energy spectrum of a many-body quantum system is a central goal of quantum physics. Ground-state energies underpin materials science and quantum chemistry, whereas excited states govern dynamical phenomena such as quantum thermalization. Quantum simulators have greatly shaped our understanding of many-body systems, for example, by enabling access to microscopic mechanisms and nonlocal order parameters. However, experiments still struggle to access the full range of many-body spectral features and are typically limited to measuring energy gaps and excitations by spectroscopic means. Here, we address this challenge by demonstrating quantum phase estimation on an analog Rydberg quantum simulator. We reconstruct the complex-valued return amplitude, or Loschmidt echo, of an initial probe state. From its Fourier transform, we measure absolute ground-state energies and energy gaps in systems of up to 19 atoms in one and two spatial dimensions. Varying the initial probe state, we select distinct spectral windows within which we compute the longitudinal and transverse magnetization, and observe their competition across the many-body spectrum. Our results thereby demonstrate phase-sensitive many-body spectroscopy on an analog quantum simulator without auxiliary qubits or controlled evolution.

Hendrik Timme, ..., Immanuel Bloch, Johannes Zeiher

item.title: [20★] Beyond Blossom: Accelerating MWPM Decoding for Surface Codes With Local Predecoding and Architecture-Aware Optimizations
item.author: Jiayu Fu, ..., Riling Li, Guangwen Yang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 20 ★

Authors: Jiayu Fu, ..., Riling Li, Guangwen Yang

arXiv ID: 2611.18476 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is widely used to decode surface codes, but its computational cost increases with code distance. We present Beyond Blossom, a state-of-the-art CPU-based MWPM decoder for surface codes. It combines algorithmic optimization through local predecoding, architecture-aware optimization, and pipeline-wide parallelism to reduce matching workload and execution overhead while preserving MWPM optimality. Across rotated surface codes with distances 9-33 and circuit-level physical error rates of 0.05%-0.3%, on a single CPU core, Beyond Blossom achieves a 4.23×\times geometric-mean speedup and up to 5.58×\times speedup over Sparse Blossom in PyMatching. At distance 33 and a physical error rate of 0.1%, with 8 CPU cores, decoding a block of 33 measurement rounds takes 21.40 μ\mus on average, equivalent to 0.65 μ\mus per round.

Jiayu Fu, ..., Riling Li, Guangwen Yang

item.title: [18★] Quantum Preparation without Disturbance: Information Costs and Hypothesis Testing
item.author: Pablo Costa Rico, ..., Mario Berta, Ángela Capel
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 18 ★

Authors: Pablo Costa Rico, ..., Mario Berta, Ángela Capel

arXiv ID: 2611.18135 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We determine the minimum information cost of preparing either of two quantum states with one common device while preserving its memory. Measured by the Umegaki relative entropy between the two possible memory states, this minimum is the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy of the target states. If the memory may instead be consumed, the minimum is their Umegaki relative entropy. More generally, for any divergence satisfying data processing, memory preservation selects the maximal extension of its classical restriction. We also study the cost of requiring only finitely many outputs, with the costs increasing from Umegaki to Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy as the number of outputs grows. Finally, we consider hypothesis testing of an unknown device over independent runs. The optimal Stein exponent per run converges to the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy whenever the number of outputs per run diverges. This gives an operational characterization of the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy in quantum statistics.

Pablo Costa Rico, ..., Mario Berta, Ángela Capel

item.title: [11★] Tessa: Encoding Classical Data Across an Entire Quantum Processor
item.author: Daniel Bultrini
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 11 ★

Authors: Daniel Bultrini

arXiv ID: 2611.18440 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We present Tessa, a hardware-aware, device-wide scheme to encode classical data on quantum computers. We use it to experimentally encode and decode up to 15681568 real values using IBM's Phoenix and Fez quantum computers on a variety of data. Tessa's construction is an extension of QPIXL and QCrank. However, it checkerboards address and data qubits across a coupling graph with neighbouring data qubits sharing only a subset of address qubits. When using the device's coupling graph no SWAP gates or routing is required, but the construction works for any bipartite coupling graph. The shots required for readout are determined by the local coupling degree. As examples, we have used cat states (pixel art of cats), various pixel art, audio, MIDI, DNA sequences and protein amino acid sequences.

Daniel Bultrini

item.title: [9★] Efficient quantum-circuit simulation of classical control of computational order
item.author: Raphaël Mothe, Jessica Bavaresco
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 9 ★

Authors: Raphaël Mothe, Jessica Bavaresco

arXiv ID: 2611.17454 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We show that quantum circuits with classical control of computational order admit an efficient simulation by fixed-order quantum circuits: any such transformation acting on NN independent quantum channels can be deterministically, exactly, and universally simulated using at most N2N^2 queries. We generalize these constructions to extended, bipartite quantum channels and quantum instruments, and demonstrate that they can be implemented catalytically, without consuming the additional N2−NN^2-N queries required for the simulation. In the case of quantum circuits with quantum control of computational order, we prove a similar simulation result, but restricted to unitary input channels (hence non-universal). These results show the limitations of the computational power of these classes of transformations in the studied scenarios.

Raphaël Mothe, Jessica Bavaresco

item.title: [7★] Compiling Matrix Formulas to Quantum Block Encodings
item.author: Daksh Shami, Charles Yuan
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 7 ★

Authors: Daksh Shami, Charles Yuan

arXiv ID: 2611.17756 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Realizing the promise of quantum applications such as chemistry or fluid dynamics requires building quantum circuits that efficiently encode and manipulate exponentially large matrices. This process forces researchers to grapple with the reality that a matrix expressible as one equation on paper can map to thousands of bit-level quantum logic gates, historically written by hand. Even worse, it often ends with a discovery that the needed resources grow so quickly with matrix size that the quantum algorithm loses its asymptotic speedup. In this work, we present MARBLE, a language that automatically synthesizes an efficient circuit from the publication-style formula for the entries of a matrix. MARBLE algebraically rewrites programs into symbolic combinations of simpler matrices that have known circuit realizations. It analyzes costs of possible representations, notably the subnormalization term that dominates time complexity. It then emits an OpenQASM circuit and certifies whether its cost is poly-logarithmic in problem size, as required by quantum algorithms. When evaluated on quantum applications ranging from fluid dynamics to physical Hamiltonians, MARBLE matches or surpasses 37 of 39 published baselines. On the low end, it automatically matches many theoretically optimal circuits, and on the high end, it improves on a published construction in fluid dynamics by 10,487x in subnormalization. MARBLE produces exponentially smaller circuits than the leading tool FABLE, and it successfully compiles matrices whose dimensions exceed 2^100 within five seconds on a laptop.

Daksh Shami, Charles Yuan

item.title: [6★] Quantum thermometry with k-local Hamiltonians
item.author: Jorge López González, ..., Anna Sanpera, María García Díaz
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Jorge López González, ..., Anna Sanpera, María García Díaz

arXiv ID: 2611.18327 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

In equilibrium quantum thermometry, the precision of temperature estimation increases with the heat capacity of the probe thermometer. For an n-body thermometer, the maximum heat capacity is attained by a Hamiltonian that requires n-local interactions, making its physical implementation challenging. In the thermodynamic limit, the optimal heat capacity scales quadratically with n. Although more experimentally accessible 2-local Hamiltonians can achieve this optimal scaling, their performance remains significantly below the theoretical maximum for realistic system sizes. Here, we restrict to this scenario and show a substantial enhancement in the thermometric performance with only a minimal increase in locality in some Hamiltonian models. We further introduce k-local generalizations of these models and show that their thermometric performance systematically approaches the theoretical optimum as the locality is increased. By analyzing their spectra, we relate this enhancement to the progressive emergence of the spectral structure underlying optimal equilibrium thermometry. Lastly, we discuss the heat capacity as a witness of Hamiltonian locality.

Jorge López González, ..., Anna Sanpera, María García Díaz

item.title: [6★] Magic of Dicke states: density, cost and yield
item.author: Yves H. Kwan
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Yves H. Kwan

arXiv ID: 2611.17623 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Dicke states are an elementary family of many-body quantum states, consisting of equal superpositions of all configurations of LL qubits with nn excitations. We show that their magic, as measured by the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), is extensive at every filling f=n/Lf=n/L except half-filling, and we obtain the magic density analytically, together with the subleading terms. In the context of fault-tolerant quantum computation, we also investigate the yield of Dicke states, and find that they can produce on average an extensive number of CCZ states (or TT states with a catalyst) at any 0<f<10<f<1. This yield is not self-averaging, but fluctuates from run to run by O(L)O(L), as if it were set by a hidden phase shared by all qubits. At half-filling, the SRE grows only logarithmically, while the preparation cost, average yield and relative entropy of magic remain extensive, so that a small SRE does not necessarily signal a weak resource. These results can be understood by viewing the Dicke state as a fixed-magnetization projection of a product of tilted spins.

Yves H. Kwan

item.title: [5★] No universal LOCC entanglement purification
item.author: C.L.Liu, Baoqing Sun, D. M. Tong
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: C.L.Liu, Baoqing Sun, D. M. Tong

arXiv ID: 2611.17809 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Entanglement purification aims to obtain high-fidelity entangled states from noisy entangled states. This task becomes particularly challenging when the available input states are finite in number, only partially characterized, and may not be identical. Whether there exists a universal purification protocol applicable to such inputs has therefore been a longstanding question. This motivates the study of universal nn-to-11 entanglement purification. Although no such LOCC protocol exists for the full set of two-qubit entangled states, it has remained open whether this no-go result extends to higher-dimensional bipartite states and multipartite states. In this work, we resolve this question by proving that, for any fixed finite local dimensions, no nn-to-11 LOCC protocol is universal for all bipartite entangled states or all multipartite entangled states. We further show that the bipartite and multipartite no-go results persist under several natural extensions and establish an analogous no-go theorem for coherence purification under strictly incoherent operations.

C.L.Liu, Baoqing Sun, D. M. Tong

item.title: [5★] Tight Quantum Query Bounds for Collision Finding over Arbitrary Bounded Types
item.author: Tianci Peng, Shiqi Hou, Xiaoyang Dong
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: Tianci Peng, Shiqi Hou, Xiaoyang Dong

arXiv ID: 2611.17804 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We determine the bounded-error quantum query complexity of finding one rr-collision in an NN-input function of prescribed type, which specifies all equality-class sizes. For every fixed maximum class size and collision order, we give a tight bound as the maximum of scales determined by the numbers of classes of size at least 2,…,r2,\ldots,r. The lower bound holds for a uniformly random function of that type, and a matching algorithm succeeds on every such function. No intermediate class size is required to occur, and every feasible output alphabet is allowed. The characterization connects the abundant-collision regime associated with set equality to the sparse-target regime of kk-distinctness. In particular, finding the unique (k+1)(k+1)-collision in type (kn,k+1)(k^n,k+1) has complexity Θk(N3/4−1/[4(2k+1−1)])\Theta_k(N^{3/4-1/[4(2^{k+1}-1)]}), where N=kn+k+1N=kn+k+1, resolving an open problem of Belovs. For the lower bound, we introduce a filtered compressed permutation oracle that projects onto a harmonic database subspace after each complete function query. Its O(T/N)O(T/N) comparison error over TT queries overcomes the square-root limitation of the unfiltered process. Hidden capacity extensions and moment estimates retain the populations at each intermediate collision order. Matching upper bounds use sampled collision lists and colored adaptive learning graphs, with a coherent decision-to-search conversion that avoids logarithmic overhead. We also give an alternative nested quantum-walk algorithm for three-collision search, matching the bound up to polylogarithmic factors.

Tianci Peng, Shiqi Hou, Xiaoyang Dong

item.title: [5★] Quantum violation of Causal Friendliness in the instrumental scenario
item.author: Emanuele Polino, ..., Eric G. Cavalcanti, Fabio Sciarrino
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: Emanuele Polino, ..., Eric G. Cavalcanti, Fabio Sciarrino

arXiv ID: 2611.17431 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

How far can quantum theory depart from a classical worldview? Bell inequality violations show that no theory can simultaneously uphold absoluteness of observed events, freedom of choice, relativistic causality, and classical causal explanations. While generalized notions of causality, capable of incorporating quantum resources, can account for Bell correlations, the Local Friendliness theorem showed that, in extended Wigner's friend scenarios, the conflict between quantum theory and causal explanations persists even after classical causality is abandoned. This revealed a new form of nonclassicality stronger than what was revealed by Bell's theorem. However, Local Friendliness has been confined to Bell causal structures so far, and it remains unknown whether a related form of nonclassicality persists in more general causal networks. Here we answer this question by considering a Wigner's friend version of the instrumental network, a paradigmatic causal structure in which communication between parties is allowed, and, unlike the Bell scenario, relativistic causality does not impose any restriction. We show, both theoretically and in a proof-of-principle photonic experiment, that quantum correlations are incompatible with Causal Friendliness, which is the conjunction of the absoluteness of observed events and the generalized nonclassical causal constraints imposed by the network. Such constraints extend relativistic causality from Bell scenarios to networks of arbitrary structure. These results establish a form of quantum nonclassicality stronger than previously observed in instrumental-network violations of classical causality, generalizing Local Friendliness beyond Bell-Wigner scenarios and uncovering a new class of correlations with potential applications in future quantum technologies.

Emanuele Polino, ..., Eric G. Cavalcanti, Fabio Sciarrino

item.title: [3★] Formulating Uncomputation Beyond Classical Ancilla Use
item.author: Bonan Su, Shengyuan Yang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Bonan Su, Shengyuan Yang

arXiv ID: 2611.18325 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Ancilla qubits are routinely used to simplify quantum circuit construction and reduce implementation costs, but their use introduces the burden of designing proper uncomputation afterward. To alleviate this, prior work has developed automated uncomputation synthesis based on a computational-basis formulation of ancilla use. However, this formulation is tailored to classically structured ancilla computations. For more general circuits, it may be undefined, yield unintended functionality, or fail to synthesize uncomputation. It therefore falls short of providing a precise and general formulation of uncomputation beyond classical ancilla use. To address these limitations, we propose a new formulation of ancilla use that specifies the operation of each gate through two complementary aspects: (1) the functionality it implements and (2) the transformation it induces on ancilla roles. Based on this specification, we define uncomputation as restoring the initial ancilla role while implementing the identity functionality. This perspective enables a simple Use-first strategy for automatically synthesizing uncomputation in cases both within and beyond the scope of prior approaches. We further develop a complete inference system for reasoning about specifications, together with a derivation-directed procedure for automatically synthesizing efficient uncomputation, enabling systematic uncomputation synthesis even in challenging cases beyond the scope of our automatic strategy.

Bonan Su, Shengyuan Yang

item.title: [3★] Fer expansion converges almost twice as far as Magnus for qubits
item.author: Lorenzo Bagnasacco, Vittorio Giovannetti
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Lorenzo Bagnasacco, Vittorio Giovannetti

arXiv ID: 2611.18249 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The Fer expansion writes the propagator of a time-dependent Hamiltonian as a product of unitary exponentials whose error decreases doubly exponentially with the number of factors, while the Magnus expansion improves by one order at a time. Its convergence, however, was guaranteed only below a radius of about 2.60582.6058, smaller than the Magnus radius π\pi. We establish a guaranteed convergence threshold of about 6.21066.2106, or 1.98π1.98\,\pi, for a qubit. This is almost twice the optimal universal Magnus threshold π\pi; the bound on a single Fer step is sharp, while the exact convergence radius remains open.

Lorenzo Bagnasacco, Vittorio Giovannetti

item.title: [3★] An Incomplete-Preference Quantum Anscombe--Aumann Representation
item.author: Cristhiano Duarte
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Cristhiano Duarte

arXiv ID: 2611.18233 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

This work develops a generalised Anscombe--Aumann framework in which acts map a finite set of states of the world into the effect interval of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, while preferences need not be complete. The construction keeps three logically distinct questions separate. First, an incomplete-preference multi-utility theorem supplies affine utility functionals. Second, finite-dimensional operator geometry determines the form of each affine functional. Third, admissibility identifies which normalised probability--state pairs are compatible with the full preference. We introduce behavioural state-independence as the natural Anscombe--Aumann interpretation of the idea that the identity of the states of the world should not affect how quantum consequences are compared. Because an incomplete preference makes this aggregate behavioural condition weaker than a utility-by-utility condition, the factorisation theorem requires a stronger, explicitly operational representation-level condition. Under that condition and Loewner monotonicity, every affine utility functional is positively affinely equivalent to a normalised utility of the form Up,ρ(f)=∑sp(s)Tr(ρf(s))U_{p,\rho}(f)=\sum_{s}p(s)Tr(\rho f(s)). Consequently, a suitable incomplete preference relation is represented by a family of admissible pairs in Δ(S)×D(H)\Delta(S) \times \mathcal{D} ( \mathcal{H} ) . We then identify a canonical maximal compatible family and show that the scalar-effect subspace carries an ordinary classical multi-utility representation, with scalar events appearing as the vertices of the scalar-act cube.

Cristhiano Duarte

item.title: [3★] Maximally Entangled Mutually Unbiased Bases in Bipartite Systems of Unequal Prime Dimensions
item.author: Bogdan S. Damski, Karol Życzkowski
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Bogdan S. Damski, Karol Życzkowski

arXiv ID: 2611.18232 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Mutually unbiased bases with prescribed entanglement properties are of fundamental interest in quantum information theory. In the interesting case of a bipartite Hilbert space of unequal prime dimensions, Hp⊗Hq\mathcal{H}_p\otimes\mathcal{H}_q, with p<qp<q prime, the standard solution provides p+1p+1 product bases. For any such dimension d=pqd=pq we construct p+1p+1 bases, such that pp of them are represented by complex Hadamard matrices, each equivalent to a Fourier matrix FdF_d, with all vectors maximally entangled. Our explicit construction is based on eigenvectors of suitable Weyl--Heisenberg operators, the Chinese Remainder Theorem and quadratic Gaussian sums. The obtained result establishes a lower bound for the number of maximally entangled mutually unbiased bases, M(p,q)≥pM(p,q)\geq p.

Bogdan S. Damski, Karol Życzkowski

item.title: [3★] Spin-adapted sample-based quantum diagonalization with randomized time evolution
item.author: Stefano Barison, ..., Francesco Tacchino, Ivano Tavernelli
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Stefano Barison, ..., Francesco Tacchino, Ivano Tavernelli

arXiv ID: 2611.18071 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum algorithms based on the classical post-processing of measurement samples have emerged as effective and robust methods to approximate low-energy wavefunctions of many-body quantum systems on present-day and early-fault-tolerant quantum devices. This paper introduces a generic framework for enforcing spin symmetry within these approaches. We tailor this framework to SqDRIFT, a sample-based quantum diagonalization variant that uses the qDRIFT randomized compilation protocol to generate the quantum samples. We discuss how three key components of SqDRIFT (the initial-state preparation, the construction of the time-evolution circuits, and the classical post-processing) can be adapted to incorporate spin symmetry. We show that spin-pure circuits alone are not sufficient, since the sampled determinants generally span a subspace that is not closed under ˆS2\hat{S}^2, and we restore this closure by completing the sampled electronic configurations. In classical simulations of 4-aminobenzonitrile and of an [Fe(NH3)4]2+[\text{Fe}(\text{NH}_{3})_{4}]^{2+} model complex, and in experiments on an IBM quantum processor for the oxo-Mn(Salen) complex, this spin-adapted post-processing yields roots that are exact spin eigenfunctions at every subspace size. On hardware, it does so with diagonalized subspaces two to three orders of magnitude smaller than those of the conventional constructions for the same circuit depth.

Stefano Barison, ..., Francesco Tacchino, Ivano Tavernelli

item.title: [3★] The cone of states over time: exact tests and convergent two-sided hierarchies
item.author: Matt Hoogsteder-Riera
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Matt Hoogsteder-Riera

arXiv ID: 2611.18001 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A state over time (stote) pairs a state ρ\rho with a channel E\mathcal{E} as the Hermitian, generally non-positive operator (ρ⊗1)⋆JE(\rho\otimes\mathbf{1})\star J_\mathcal{E}. We study the convex cone ˆQ\widehat{\mathcal{Q}} generated by these operators. Our main result is a convergent outer semidefinite hierarchy with an explicit trace-norm Hausdorff bound on its trace-one slices. item.title: [3★] Indefinite causal order with definite Bohmian trajectories for the quantum switch
item.author: Aurélien Drezet
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Aurélien Drezet

arXiv ID: 2611.17906 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We analyze the notion of indefinite causal order (ICO) from the standpoint of the deterministic de Broglie--Bohm theory, based on the notion of trajectories in configuration space. More precisely, we study the physics of the quantum switch (QS) interferometer within a Bohmian framework and show how the notion of causality is preserved in this approach. Furthermore, we investigate device-independent certification and causal inequalities applied to an entangled quantum system, and show that in this regime too, the notions of trajectories and of a strict causal order are perfectly preserved.

Aurélien Drezet

item.title: [2★] Entanglement and information dynamics in charged dual-unitary circuits with impurities
item.author: Shachar Fraenkel, Colin Rylands
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Shachar Fraenkel, Colin Rylands

arXiv ID: 2611.18435 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Local parts of a closed, non-equilibrium quantum many-body system can reach stationarity through the buildup of entanglement between different regions. In this paper we investigate how this process is affected by the presence of a quantum impurity that breaks a global symmetry of the bulk. In particular, we study a charged dual-unitary quantum circuit perturbed by a symmetry-breaking, non-dual-unitary gate acting on a spatially fixed pair of sites. In this setup we calculate the entanglement entropy for a subsystem that does not contain the impurity, as well as the mutual information and logarithmic negativity for a bipartite subsystem that straddles the impurity. We obtain exact results in the early time regime for these quantities from the dual unitarity of the bulk system. Beyond this regime, we compute the predictions of the quasiparticle and entanglement membrane pictures, supporting them with exact calculations obtained by taking the corresponding limits of the bulk entangling power. We find that the presence of a symmetry-breaking impurity can lead to a richer behaviour of quantum relaxation, including non-monotonic evolution of the entanglement entropy, a modification of the long-time steady state, and persistent subsystem mutual information and entanglement negativity. This behaviour is understood in terms of long-range correlations generated by scattering from the impurity, and facilitated by the ballistic propagation of the conserved charges.

Shachar Fraenkel, Colin Rylands

item.title: [2★] Transfer-Matrix Calculus for Infinite Matrix Product States
item.author: Qi Yang, Philippe Corboz
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Qi Yang, Philippe Corboz

arXiv ID: 2611.18427 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Long-range interactions, from the Coulomb repulsion between electrons to the power-law interactions of trapped ions and Rydberg atoms, are widespread in quantum many-body physics. For infinite systems, however, MPS algorithms, the standard classical reference in one dimension, conventionally rely on a computational compromise: replacing these interactions by fitted sums of exponentials. We develop transfer-matrix calculus (TMC), a unified framework for deriving infinite-MPS algorithms. In TMC, an interaction is written as a function of the transfer matrix, and one set of contraction rules then yields the effective Hamiltonians of DMRG and VUMPS, the tangent-space excitation action, and the energy variance, without an MPO. Long-range interactions thus enter with their prescribed distance dependence. For the half-filled lattice Coulomb chain with a 1/d1/d interaction of strength VV, theory predicts CDW order for all V>0V>0, but at weak coupling this order is too weak for earlier numerics to resolve. Using TMC, we obtain infinite-MPS ground states at V=2V=2 directly in the thermodynamic limit, with an energy variance per site of 2×10−102\times10^{-10}. Our data, extrapolated to zero energy variance, indicate a small nonzero CDW amplitude, m0=0.002213(14)m_0=0.002213(14), consistent with this prediction. The complete V=2V=2 optimization workflow across the full series of bond dimensions takes less than a day on a single AMD MI250X GPU die. For an exactly solvable long-range hopping model, TMC reproduces the nonanalytic |k||k| cusp of the one-particle dispersion that any fixed finite sum of decaying exponentials rounds off. We also use TMC to optimize first-quantized MPS directly in the thermodynamic limit. For half-filled free fermions, our entanglement entropy data show scaling consistent with central charge c=1c=1 over the studied bond dimensions, as for second-quantized MPS.

Qi Yang, Philippe Corboz

item.title: [2★] Entropic quantum error correction for independent and correlated amplitude damping errors
item.author: Gang Zhou
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Gang Zhou

arXiv ID: 2611.18192 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The idea of using quantum entropy for quantum error correction (QEC) has existed for a long time. However, its computational complexity has limited its practical use: even a [[4,1]][[4,1]] code for standard independent amplitude damping errors involves a 256×256256\times 256 Hermitian matrix, so the approach scales poorly as the codeword length increases. For correlated errors, the situation is even worse. In this paper, we show that, by using the insights developed in our previous paper and exploiting certain structures of quantum conditional mutual information, we can solve these problems exactly by hand, using only 2×22\times 2 unitary matrices. By examining the entropy, we identify the leakage channels and the amount of leakage exactly, then define the recovery map accordingly. The rules defining our recovery map are simple, intuitive, and computationally inexpensive: for independent errors, it is based on 16 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions; for correlated errors, it is based on 6 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions. Our method sacrifices little in terms of performance: for the widely used entanglement fidelity, our simple QEC recovery map achieves a sharp result; for the worst-case fidelity, the best result is about 9%9\% better than ours; for correlated errors, there are no comparable results for short codewords. Among the known techniques, our recovery map is the first non-global one. The calculations use elementary linear algebra and calculus, and is presented in great detail.

Gang Zhou

item.title: [2★] Benchmarking superconducting quantum processors with percolating entanglement quality
item.author: Akinori Machino, ..., Arvind Mamgain, et al (4)
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Akinori Machino, ..., Arvind Mamgain, et al (4)

arXiv ID: 2611.17941 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The capability to create large entanglement resources is a key performance attribute of quantum processors, and the size of the resource is often used as a benchmark of processor scale. Recent graph-state experiments have reported entanglement clusters spanning entire chips with hundreds of qubits. However, cluster size alone does not capture the entanglement quality of individual couplings or differences in coupling topology. Here, we introduce percolating entanglement quality (PEQ), a topology-normalized benchmark based on conditional two-qubit negativity and a topology-specific bond-percolation threshold. As an experimental demonstration, we prepare a native graph state on a 64-qubit square-lattice superconducting processor with defects, identify a 52-qubit entanglement cluster, and evaluate the PEQ of the processor. Applying PEQ to previously reported chip-wide graph-state measurements on heavy-hex-lattice processors, we show that PEQ differs substantially among processors whose entanglement clusters span the entire chip. PEQ provides a single chip-wide score without selecting a best-performing qubit subset or path. This score allows processors with different coupling topologies to be compared on a common scale and can inform the design of coupling topologies for scalable chips.

Akinori Machino, ..., Arvind Mamgain, et al (4)

item.title: [2★] Quantum Data Processing Unit for Neutral-Atom Quantum Computers
item.author: Pranav Srinivas Murali, ..., Anil Bilgin, Yi-Zhuang You
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Pranav Srinivas Murali, ..., Anil Bilgin, Yi-Zhuang You

arXiv ID: 2611.17652 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum computers need real-time classical processing to convert measurement data into feedback within device-specific timing constraints. We introduce the quantum data processing unit (QDPU), an architecture between a quantum device and its controller. Its core is a machine-learned quantum data model (QDM), adapted to the measurement response and noise characteristics of the device. We implement an FPGA pipeline for neutral-atom array assembly that performs occupancy detection and rearrangement scheduling in FPGA logic. One calibrated matched-filter lane classifies a 50×5050\times50 array in 12.5 μ\mus. An atom-loss model using a software reference planner evaluates a 35×3535\times35 target with a 60 s trap lifetime and 0.1% loss per moved atom. Removing an assumed 150 ms host round trip raises the predicted assembly success from 8% to 85% and reduces the wall-clock time per successful assembly from 19 s to 0.16 s. A GPU-based outer loop is proposed for refitting model parameters between runs. Its NVQLink transport is measured on the board: over 10 GbE to an NVIDIA DGX Spark, the median FPGA-to-host-to-FPGA round trip is 2.74 μ\mus for 128-byte messages forwarded by a CPU core. A separate 12-bit learned qLDPC kernel is placed and routed for the same FPGA target, with a derived latency of 0.84 ms per round for a [[1122,148]][[1122,148]] lifted-product code under code-capacity noise. A quantised GraphMP ranking kernel for the same code runs on the board with a median host-to-FPGA-to-host latency of 50.5 μ\mus with one shot in flight, excluding host-side BP+OSD post-processing. Together, these implementations illustrate a shared architecture with workload-specific models and timing requirements.

item.title: [2★] QuantumInputOutput.jl: A Julia framework for input-output theory with quantum pulses and the SLH formalism
item.author: Christoph Hotter, Orjan Ameye, Klaus Mølmer
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Christoph Hotter, Orjan Ameye, Klaus Mølmer

arXiv ID: 2611.17451 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The interaction of traveling photonic pulses with quantum systems is a fundamental process for many quantum technologies such as quantum communication, control, and measurement protocols. The so-called SLH formalism, named for the triple of operators that parametrize the dynamics, in combination with virtual emission and absorption cavities provides a general toolbox to describe such processes. However, modeling open quantum systems driven by propagating quantum pulses becomes cumbersome once several components, channels, and temporal modes are involved. Here we present QuantumInputOutput.jl, an open-source framework that automates this derivation process: first, symbolic expressions for the Hamiltonian and Lindblad operators are derived using predefined SLH rules and symbolic quantum algebra. Next, the obtained operators are converted to (time-dependent) numerical matrices or are used to obtain higher-order mean-field equations. The numerical expressions are presented in a form immediately suitable for solving the time evolution of the master equation and analyzing the output modes via correlation functions. Besides its usefulness for numerical simulations, the framework also provides a convenient tool to derive symbolic expressions for one-dimensional quantum systems such as multilevel emitters in cavities or waveguides.

Christoph Hotter, Orjan Ameye, Klaus Mølmer

item.title: [1★] Real-time simulation of scattering in ϕ4\phi^4 theory: localized excitation, scalable wave packet preparation, and peak-generating artifacts
item.author: Boyu Gao, Natalie Klco
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Boyu Gao, Natalie Klco

arXiv ID: 2611.18552 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Probing real-time dynamics is essential for understanding non-perturbative scattering and interactions in quantum field theory. A common challenge in real-time simulation is preparing accurate asymptotic incoming states. Through efficiently solvable eigenvalue problems, we jointly optimize a superposition of single particle momentum eigenstates and a single site interpolating operator to maximize preparation fidelity from the interacting vacuum. This leads to a localized excitation in the interacting theory analogous to a position eigenstate. Weighted sums of the resulting interpolating operator over lattice sites prepare wave packets of arbitrary spatial extent. To ensure that this construction produces the correct continuum limit, relative phases among single particle momentum eigenstates in this superposition are calibrated using a relation derived from Lorentz symmetry. Analyzing single particle wave packet propagation through the position space profile reveals oscillatory Airy distortions, which originate from interference between saddle point contributions at different momenta that share the same lattice group velocity. These oscillations systematically weaken when approaching the continuum limit, and reliable regimes are identified as a function of simulation time and wave packet momentum profile. Two-particle scattering simulations in interacting scalar field theory are also implemented, revealing artificial inelasticity arising from coarse local field digitization or deviation from the Nyquist-Shannon sampling point. With these artifacts under control, present simulations provide emerging evidence for physical inelastic processes in ϕ4\phi^4 theory. The constructions introduced in this work may provide new understanding of state preparation for the quantum simulation of scattering.

Boyu Gao, Natalie Klco

item.title: [1★] Structure makes quantum circuits trainable
item.author: Wenbo Xie, Wojciech Szpankowski, Ananth Grama
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Wenbo Xie, Wojciech Szpankowski, Ananth Grama

arXiv ID: 2611.18378 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The scalability of variational quantum algorithms is limited by barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in system size. This worst-case result raises fundamental questions about the trainability of quantum AI models. We present a major advance towards resolving this trainability question by answering whether a given quantum circuit has a barren plateau. We do this using an analytical framework that bounds the gradient variance for arbitrary input states ρ\rho and observables M\mathcal{M} by decomposing the unitary representation of the associated compact Lie group. When the circuit segments on both sides of a gate form 22-designs, we obtain the variance exactly and prove a sufficient condition for trainability: if ρ⊗2\rho^{\otimes 2} and M⊗2\mathcal{M}^{\otimes 2} are sufficiently concentrated on the same irreducible invariant subspace of polynomial dimension, and the differentiated gate moves this subspace by an inverse-polynomial amount, then the gradient variance is at least inverse-polynomial. We further present a sampling algorithm that estimates the gradient variance from runs of the ansatz, without constructing the representation-theoretic projectors. Our algorithm decides whether the variance exceeds a tolerance τ\tau with the number of runs polynomial in 1/τ1/\tau, including cases in which the bounds are inconclusive. This resolves the question of the trainability of the circuit before expensive training procedures.

Wenbo Xie, Wojciech Szpankowski, Ananth Grama

item.title: [1★] A Concise Introduction to Quantum Electromagnetics
item.author: Wei E. I. Sha
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Wei E. I. Sha

arXiv ID: 2611.17988 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

This book introduces quantum electromagnetics to readers trained in classical electromagnetics, without assuming a systematic background in quantum mechanics. The central question is when classical descriptions suffice, and when the quantum states of matter or the field must be retained explicitly. Starting from familiar electromagnetic modes and material response, the discussion develops atomic dynamics, field quantization, and the interaction of quantized fields with quantum matter. Particular attention is given to how mode profiles, Green functions, and scattering matrices obtained from classical electromagnetic calculations enter quantum models. Atomic coherence, photon statistics, spontaneous emission, and cavity coupling are developed through derivations that identify the physical assumptions and limits of each description. Examples drawn from atomic clocks, Rydberg-atom receivers, and single-photon devices connect these concepts to excitation, propagation, and measurement in practical systems. Loss and noise are included in relating internal dynamics to measured signals and correlations. The final discussion examines how sensitivity and claims of quantum advantage depend on bandwidth, measurement resources, and the classical reference used for comparison. The aim is to help readers choose an appropriate model, carry out the calculation, and understand what its predictions mean for an electromagnetic measurement.

Wei E. I. Sha

item.title: [1★] Multitime Equilibration and Multitime Mpemba Effects
item.author: He Wang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: He Wang

arXiv ID: 2611.17749 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Equilibration of a quantum state leaves open whether its response to later interventions has also equilibrated. We establish multitime equilibration for a continuous process on a fixed observation window, retaining the autonomous system--environment dynamics and all internal time differences. A finite-time mean-square bound controls the full continuous-process norm through the effective energy dimension and energy-gap correlations. A factorial temporal-order bound lifts fixed-sector convergence to the full process, while a process-visible spectral measure distinguishes mean-square from pointwise equilibration. This framework defines multitime Mpemba effects by comparing preparations relative to one stationary process. In a semicircle-spectrum model, a preparation filter changes the decay exponent from 3/23/2 to 5/25/2 in every fixed sector and in the summed norm, despite a larger initial distance. A fixed unitary control and terminal measurement exhibit the same exponent improvement in their output probabilities. Noncommuting baths and a many-body spin environment separate this all-sector mechanism from selective finite-time acceleration.

He Wang

item.title: [1★] Note on quantum optimal measurements of CMB spectral distortions
item.author: Roshni Singh, Jacques Delabrouille, Daniel Carney
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Roshni Singh, Jacques Delabrouille, Daniel Carney

arXiv ID: 2611.17552 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

As quantum sensing techniques continue to push the frontier of detection of ultra-weak signals, one may wonder if a sophisticated quantum strategy could be used to enable measurement of spectral distortions in the cosmic microwave background. Using quantum Fisher information techniques, we prove that the optimal strategy is simple frequency-binned intensity measurement. This proof strategy also enables us to provide numerical estimates for the information-theoretic minimum observation time required to observe the μ\mu- and yy-distortions expected from Λ\LambdaCDM cosmology. As case studies, we compare these results to the PIXIE and SPECTER mission concepts, and show that they are within a few orders of magnitude of this fundamental limit.

Roshni Singh, Jacques Delabrouille, Daniel Carney

item.title: [1★] Recursive Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz
item.author: Lennart Binkowski, Stuart Flannigan
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Lennart Binkowski, Stuart Flannigan

arXiv ID: 2611.17537 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The recursive quantum approximate optimisation algorithm~(RQAOA) shrinks an unconstrained combinatorial optimisation problem by eliminating one variable at a time, guided by correlations measured in variational quantum states. We extend this recursion to constrained problems by building on the quantum alternating operator ansatz, which restricts the evolution to feasible solutions through a feasible initial state and feasibility-preserving mixers. However, every elimination alters the feasibility structure, so that such a mixer for the original problem generally fails to be one for the subproblems. Previous extensions to Maximum Independent Set and Minimum Vertex Cover sidestep this with tailored reduction rules that keep every subproblem within the original problem class. We resolve this by identifying, for a given constraint structure, a broader problem class that is closed under all eliminations, and by efficiently constructing feasible initial states and feasibility-preserving mixers for every class member. We do so for monotone constraints, such as for the knapsack problem, for linear equality constraints with polynomially bounded weights, including Hamming weight constraints, and for combinations of equality constraints with a single inequality constraint, such as the cardinality-constrained knapsack problem. Conversely, we show that these restrictions cannot be lifted in general without leaving the realm of efficient constructions. Exact simulations on knapsack and vertex-weighted max-bisection instances demonstrate that our recursive scheme can outperform both its non-recursive counterpart and penalty-based QAOA and RQAOA.

Lennart Binkowski, Stuart Flannigan

item.title: [0★] Complex fluid flow dynamics by bright scattershot boson sampling
item.author: Robert Schade, ..., Christine Silberhorn, Jörg Schumacher
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Robert Schade, ..., Christine Silberhorn, Jörg Schumacher

arXiv ID: 2611.18510 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Boson sampling machines have become a fruitful tool for establishing new concepts, which connect fundamental physics with computer science applications. Here, we exploit the intrinsically high-dimensional correlations generated by the measurement outcomes of a multiphoton boson sampling machine and demonstrate how a reconfigurable architecture can be programmed to autonomously model the time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems that describe complex fluid flows. By extending on the original scattershot boson sampling (SBS) scheme to include higher photon number components -- a scheme which we label bright scattershot boson sampling (BSBS) --- this scheme overcomes scaling issues inherent to SBS-based schemes by utilizing all randomly generated input photon number distributions. We illustrate the capability of this scheme for two complex fluid-flow models: an eight-dimensional Lorenz-type model of two-dimensional thermally driven convection and a 16-dimensional model of global atmospheric circulation. Using a digital twin of the BSBS architecture based on multiphoton statistics, we show that the photonic approach accurately reproduces the temporal dynamics of both systems while being resilient to photon losses of up to 50 per cent. We also verified that the BSBS case outperforms a comparable run with coherent light. Moreover, its prediction horizon exceeds that of a classical reservoir-computing model with the same query complexity. These results highlight the potential of near-term photonic quantum computing for addressing relevant real-world tasks on noisy intermediate-scale devices.

Robert Schade, ..., Christine Silberhorn, Jörg Schumacher

item.title: [0★] Solution of the Qubit Marginal Problem from Fermionic Representability
item.author: David A. Mazziotti
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: David A. Mazziotti

arXiv ID: 2611.18503 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Whether local reduced states are compatible with a global quantum state---the quantum marginal problem---is central to quantum information and simulation. Here we present a solution to the ensemble marginal problem for qubits based on the representability theory of fermions. Encoding each qubit as one fermion in two orbitals, we prove that the representable qubit marginals form an exposed face of the set of NN-representable fermionic reduced density matrices, selected by the vanishing of every site-occupation variance. Complete hierarchies of fermionic representability conditions therefore transfer exactly to qubits. Applications to frustrated Heisenberg and transverse-field Ising rings show that the (2,3)(2,3)-positivity conditions are exact at the Majumdar--Ghosh point and accurate to about 0.5% at criticality. Because the conditions hold for any quantum state, they also provide a framework for mitigating measurement errors on qubit-based quantum devices.

David A. Mazziotti

item.title: [0★] Dissipation as a Resource for Entanglement via High-Spin Mediator Purification
item.author: Ellen Martins Fernandes, Fabricio Macedo de Souza
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Ellen Martins Fernandes, Fabricio Macedo de Souza

arXiv ID: 2611.18489 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We study entanglement generation between two spin qubits mediated by a single, thermally mixed, high-spin (S=5/2S=5/2) magnetic impurity, using the Lindblad master equation to compare coherent and dissipative control of the mediator. We show that no coherent drive, however strong or resonant, can purify the mediator beyond its thermal value --- a direct consequence of unitary evolution exactly preserving state purity --- while a dissipative channel purifies it up to the limit set by the optical pumping cycle itself, Tr[ρ2M]≈0.8\mathrm{Tr}[\rho_M^2]\approx0.8. Modeling this channel with rates fixed by the measured optical pumping of a single Mn spin, we find that the entanglement it enables is not monotonic in the pump strength: it peaks at a finite rate and then decreases, since the same channel leaks decoherence to the qubits through the coupling that mediates their entanglement. At the experimental pumping rate, a single 8080ns pulse purifies the mediator, the resulting polarization persists for a timescale three orders of magnitude longer than the entangling dynamics, and the first-recurrence negativity rises from 0.180.18 to 0.640.64 at 1212K, remaining above 0.60.6 up to 3030K. These results establish dissipation, not as noise to be suppressed, but as the very resource that makes robust entanglement generation possible.

item.title: [0★] Symmetry-Controlled Quantum State Transfer in Poly-bi-[8]-annulenylene: From Heisenberg to Hubbard Dynamics
item.author: Adnan Jaljuli, ..., Ammar Ali, Sabre Kais
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Adnan Jaljuli, ..., Ammar Ali, Sabre Kais

arXiv ID: 2611.18457 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We investigate quantum state transfer in the poly-bi-[8]-annulenylene lattice using isotropic Heisenberg and Hubbard models. For a 16-site lattice, reflection symmetry separates the single-excitation Hamiltonian into independent triplet and singlet sectors, allowing analytical determination of the energy spectra. Although perfect state transfer is forbidden for positive couplings, appropriately chosen coupling ratios enable pretty-good transfer with arbitrarily high fidelity. Remarkably, the triplet transfer probability is independent of the interchain rung coupling, while singlet transfer can be selectively enhanced or suppressed, enabling symmetry-selective quantum transport without time-dependent control. Extending the analysis to the Hubbard model, we show that the Heisenberg transfer dynamics emerge in the strong-interaction limit, while finite interactions delay all high-fidelity transfer peaks of a symmetry sector by the same fraction of their transfer time, set by the spectrum, and reduce the peak fidelity, even at the corrected time, by an amount that grows with the transfer time. These findings are relevant to future quantum-network architectures, where symmetry-controlled state transfer could provide a building block for connecting quantum memories and emitter-based interfaces within quantum nodes. Overall, our results demonstrate how molecular network geometry and symmetry can be exploited to engineer and control quantum-state transport in interacting spin systems, providing a theoretical framework for quantum information transfer in molecular-inspired quantum architectures.

item.title: [0★] Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments
item.author: Yuehaw Khoo, ..., Yuguan Wang, Siyao Yang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Yuehaw Khoo, ..., Yuguan Wang, Siyao Yang

arXiv ID: 2611.18448 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable. Exploiting the spatial decay of time-lagged correlations, these matrices can be approximated in sparse-plus-low-rank form using trajectory samples, with computational cost scaling linearly in the system dimension and the number of trajectories. The learning error can be further reduced by correcting the memory effect induced by the Galerkin projection. We numerically demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in extrapolating the dynamics of various many-body systems, including Langevin and Glauber dynamics for classical systems as well as Lindblad dynamics for open quantum systems. In addition, for a class of single-site Glauber dynamics, we establish error bounds for sparse-plus-low-rank compression and uniform-in-time bounds for connected-cluster approximation and observable propagation with compressed transition moment matrices.

item.title: [0★] Nesting in additive manufacturing using quantum annealing
item.author: Xiangqian Wua, ..., Marcel Wagner, Jan C. Aurich
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Xiangqian Wua, ..., Marcel Wagner, Jan C. Aurich

arXiv ID: 2611.18447 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Nesting in powder bed fusion (PBF), an additive manufacturing (AM) process, determines the positions and orientations of parts within the build space and influences build height and build time. As the number of parts and feasible placements increases, the nesting problem becomes computationally demanding. Exact approaches are limited to small problem sizes as computational effort increases rapidly with the problem size, while heuristic and metaheuristic approaches involve a trade-off between solution quality and computation time. Quantum annealing (QA) offers an alternative for solving combinatorial optimization problems, but its application to nesting in AM remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a QA-based approach for nesting in AM to investigate its feasibility and its scaling behavior across three problem sizes. An iterative binary quadratic model based approach (IBQM) is developed to minimize build height while considering the geometric characteristics of AM parts. Geometric abstraction, iterative decomposition, and variable pruning are applied to address the computational complexity of the nesting problem. The approach is evaluated using three cases with increasing problem sizes and compared to a classical approach combining tabu search and simulated annealing (TBSA). Compared with TBSA, IBQM reduces the build height of the original parts by up to 13.32% and the computation time by up to 74.27%.

item.title: [0★] Number fluctuations and particle loss in Dicke superradiance
item.author: Christian Niehof, Nico S. Bassler, Claudiu Genes
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Christian Niehof, Nico S. Bassler, Claudiu Genes

arXiv ID: 2611.18413 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Dicke superradiance, the collective spontaneous emission of identical quantum emitters into a common reservoir, produces a burst with a characteristic delay tSRt_{\mathrm{SR}} and a peak intensity that scales quadratically with the emitter number NN. This strong dependence makes the burst sensitive to how many emitters actually participate. In experiments, however, this number is rarely fixed: it fluctuates between preparations and decreases during emission through atom loss. Here we extend the analytical treatment of superradiance to variable emitter numbers using the Schwinger-boson mapping of the collective spin onto two bosonic modes. In this formulation, collective decay annihilates an atom in the excited-state mode and creates one in the ground-state mode. We find that number fluctuations enhance emission and that the ensemble-averaged emission trace encodes the initial number distribution. We show how to reconstruct second-order correlations from photon counting with finite detection efficiency and temporal resolution, even when the full distribution cannot be resolved. For atom loss at rate rr, we derive exact results for the population dynamics and show that the peak intensity scaling is governed by the single scaling variable gr=rtSRg_{\mathrm{r}}=r t_{\mathrm{SR}}. The peak remains quadratic in NN for gr<1g_{\mathrm{r}}<1, follows logarithmically corrected subquadratic power laws for gr>1g_{\mathrm{r}}>1, and crosses over to linear scaling under strong loss with gr≫1g_{\mathrm{r}}\gg1.

item.title: [0★] Quantum computational spectroscopy of complex resonances and optical residues
item.author: Payman Mahmoudi, ..., Alexander Yosifov, Jinzhao Sun
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Payman Mahmoudi, ..., Alexander Yosifov, Jinzhao Sun

arXiv ID: 2611.18388 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Optical spectra of dissipative molecular systems depend on both complex resonance energies and the way each resonance couples to an optical probe. In a non-Hermitian description, these con- tributions are determined by complex residues involving left and right eigenvectors. We introduce a quantum protocol that reconstructs the resonance poles and their biorthogonal optical residues within a common spectral-filtering and measurement framework. A Hermitian dilation embeds the left and right eigenvectors into a zero-energy subspace. Gaussian-filtered correlators evaluated with unitary circuits, together with ratios of complex off-diagonal measurements, yield the residues with- out separate variational optimisation of the eigenstates. We demonstrate spectral reconstruction for dissipative plasmon-molecule models on IBM quantum hardware, resolving how probe-dependent modal contributions produce interference-induced doublets or accompany a separation of resonance energies. We also analyse the sensitivity of residue reconstruction near exceptional points. By mak- ing complex optical residues an explicit computational output, the protocol connects non-Hermitian eigenstructure to measurable optical response.

item.title: [0★] Efficient Parameter Estimation through Quantum Extreme Learning
item.author: Dingwei Zhao, ..., Marco G. Genoni, Abolfazl Bayat
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Dingwei Zhao, ..., Marco G. Genoni, Abolfazl Bayat

arXiv ID: 2611.18329 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum sensing protocols rely on the efficient processing of measurement outcomes to infer unknown physical parameters. Conventional optimal estimators, such as Bayesian inference and maximum likelihood estimation, require to construct a likelihood function whose efficient classical construction requires full knowledge of the dynamics, which may practically be infeasible. Model-free experimental construction of the likelihood is also very resource intensive. Here, we propose a quantum extreme learning-based framework for quantum parameter estimation which avoids the explicit construction of the likelihood function. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach using the transverse-field Ising model for estimating the external transverse field. Our results show that high estimation accuracy can be achieved using measurements at only a small number of training points. We further develop an interrogation-time optimization strategy that minimizes the estimation inaccuracy while keeping sampling fluctuations below a prescribed threshold. We further extend the framework to a two-time measurement protocol, in which measurement outcomes obtained at two distinct times are combined to enrich the feature space, thereby significantly enhancing the estimation accuracy. Our analysis shows that the estimation precision improves monotonically with the number of training points, while increasing the system size generally enhances the sensing performance, albeit non-monotonically. Finally, the protocol is shown to be robust against dephasing, making it suitable for near-term quantum devices.

Abstract:

Abstract:

Whether gravity has quantum degrees of freedom is a question of fundamental importance. We formulate a linear monitoring-feedback framework for gravitational interactions that includes local classical-record models of semiclassical gravity and, when quantum resources are supplied in correlated ancilla inputs, can reproduce linearized quantum-gravity dynamics. Auxiliary systems monitor the positions of massive bodies, and their records are fed back through a chosen gravitational response kernel. At the level of linear input-output theory, this construction makes the deterministic response explicit while exposing the force noise and correlations associated with the auxiliary sector. We organize the allowed ancilla correlations into three regimes. In Regime-I, independent ancillas have unsqueezed, uncorrelated sensing and back-action quadratures. In Regime-II, arbitrary local sensing--back-action correlations are allowed, but the ancillas associated with different objects remain independent. The single-object CGN is then unrestricted, while the joint force-noise matrix obeys a determinant bound that is equivalent to the local classical-channel/no-entanglement bound. In Regime-III, cross-object correlations and a common nonlocal mediator are allowed. The commuting force noises can then be jointly squeezed, entanglement between the masses can occur, and--with a suitable retarded response and input state--the monitoring-feedback system can reproduce the noise and commutators of linearized quantum gravity, including non-Markovian quantum fluctuations.

Abstract:

Abstract:

The radical pair mechanism is a quantum-mechanical process underlying weak magnetic field effects in chemical and biological systems. While nuclear polarization and electronic entanglement in this mechanism have been studied extensively, the possibility of creating entanglement between nuclear spins has, to the best of our knowledge, remained unexplored. Abstract:

Although it was proposed almost 70 years ago, the electric version of the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect, where the interference pattern of quantum charged particles is affected by electric fields that do not interact locally with them, was never experimentally implemented. Abstract:

The spread complexity characterizes the spreading of a quantum state over the Krylov basis and has been proposed to capture the correlations between energy levels. How such correlations manifest in the dynamics has been studied mainly numerically for large matrices. Abstract:
